name: שברים חלקיים – פירוק ואז אינטגרל, גורם חוזר וחילוק (2 סעיפים, באנגלית)
questiontext:
a

Write

\[ {{CT:0}} \]

as partial fractions.

[[input:ap]]
[[validation:ap]]
[[feedback:partfrac]]
b

Find

\[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}}. \]

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:Result]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The degree of the numerator equals the degree of the denominator: divide first, then decompose the remaining proper fraction into partial fractions (cover-up and comparing coefficients), and integrate term by term.
Step 1 — Long division
Since the degree of the numerator is equal to the degree of the denominator, we need to use long division:

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}} + {{CT:3}}. \]

Step 2 — Partial fractions
The remaining proper fraction has the linear factor \({{CT:4}}\) and the repeated factor \({{CT:5}}\) in its denominator, so
Partial fractions: \( \frac{p(x)}{(x-a)(x-b)}=\frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{x-b} \); a repeated factor \( (x-a)^2 \) gives \( \frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{(x-a)^2} \); an irreducible \( x^2+bx+c \) gives \( \frac{Ax+B}{x^2+bx+c} \)

\[ {{CT:2}} = \frac{A}{{{CT:4}}}+\frac{B}{{{CT:6}}}+\frac{C}{{{CT:5}}} \]

Multiplying both sides by the denominator \({{CT:7}}\) gives

\[ {{CT:8}} = A\,{{CT:5}}+B\,{{CT:9}}+C\left({{CT:4}}\right) \]

Substituting \({{CT:1}}={{CT:10}}\) makes the \(B\) and \(C\) terms vanish:

\[ {{CT:11}} = A\cdot {{CT:12}}\quad\Rightarrow\quad A={{CT:13}} \]

Substituting \({{CT:1}}={{CT:14}}\) makes the \(A\) and \(B\) terms vanish:

\[ {{CT:15}} = C\cdot \left({{CT:16}}\right)\quad\Rightarrow\quad C={{CT:17}} \]

Comparing the coefficients of \({{CT:1}}^2\) on both sides:

\[ {{CT:18}} = A+B\quad\Rightarrow\quad B={{CT:19}} \]

Hence, using partial fractions we have

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:20}}. \]

This is the answer to part a.
Step 3 — Integrating term by term
So,

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int {{CT:20}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:13}} \int {{CT:21}} d{{CT:1}} + {{CT:19}} \int {{CT:22}} d{{CT:1}} + {{CT:17}} \int \left({{CT:23}}\right) d{{CT:1}} + \int {{CT:3}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:24}} + {{CT:25}} + {{CT:26}}+ {{CT:27}} + c \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:28}}+c \end{array} \]
